threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube'—locals just say 'the Overground' if they even bother. It’s the little things that give you away.
Last night on the 78, a guy serenaded the whole bus with acoustic covers. The driver didn’t even flinch. Only in Bermondsey, I swear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I saw a group of friends using an old tram stop for a barbecue, complete with a portable speaker and disco lights. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you catch a bus that stops for a pop-up art show in the middle of the street. They just block traffic and let it happen.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to avoid BART during delays but still complain about Muni’s dog incidents like it’s a personal affront.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni near Civic Center today and a dog just settled down on the tracks like it owned the place. Classic San Francisco chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think the plaça is just for photos. They miss the locals using it as a godsend for kids' soccer games on weekends.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their confusion at the festa major: they’re still chowing down on churros while the locals are already on to the next round of vermut.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can always spot the newcomers—they're the ones still trying to figure out the bus routes instead of just embracing the night buses.
Caught a guy on the 333 arguing with his reflection in the window, convinced it was a rival. Brixton really brings out the characters at night.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the guy in an avocado suit arguing with a pigeon over bread crumbs at Hermannplatz, I thought, 'Yep, this is home.'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous techno party in a laundromat at 3 AM, complete with spinning washers and a DJ on the countertop.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Locals know the best taco spots can have a line out the door, but the waiter's smile fades at the mention of pouring rain.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo deep in a Muni nap, drooling on his bow tie. Classic SF—always a surprise around every corner.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the vibrant murals here pop up overnight, but most are painted over carefully, some taking weeks to get just right.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still search for the right metro line on their phone, even when locals glide straight to the platform.
